back: Verification proves ownership via a DNS record and is what makes a domain usable at all. Primary only picks the default UPN suffix offered in the creation form. Keyword: default, not restriction.
Scopes a role assignment to a subset of users, groups, or devices. The answer to 'helpdesk for one office only'. Keyword: scope.
Blocks tenant-scoped role holders from modifying the members, so only administrators scoped to the AU can manage them. Keyword: protect from tenant admins.
Security controls access to resources. Microsoft 365 additionally provisions a mailbox, SharePoint site, and Teams team. Keyword: collaboration workloads.
A rule over attributes; the service recalculates membership when attributes change. Requires Entra ID P1. Keyword: no manual maintenance.
Must be set at creation and cannot be added later. Required before a group can hold a directory role. Keyword: at creation only.
Members inherit the licence and lose it on removal. Fails per user on missing prerequisites or exhausted seats. Keyword: inherit and release.
Defined in attribute sets, hidden from ordinary admins, and need dedicated Attribute Definition or Attribute Assignment roles. Keyword: not readable by default.
The guest authenticates against their home tenant; your directory holds only a guest object. Keyword: no credential in your tenant.
Accept the partner's MFA, compliant-device, or hybrid-joined claim so guests are not challenged twice. Keyword: trust their claim.
Provisions users from one tenant into another automatically and keeps them in step. For multi-tenant organisations, not occasional partners. Keyword: provision, not invite.

front: Entra Connect Sync vs Cloud Sync
back: Cloud Sync is lightweight, cloud-managed, and handles multiple disconnected forests. Connect Sync is needed for device writeback and complex filtering. Keyword: new deployments start with Cloud Sync.
Password hash sync authenticates in the cloud and survives an on-premises outage. Pass-through validates against a domain controller and depends on the agent. Keyword: outage resilience.
The single modern place methods are enabled and targeted at groups. Replaces legacy per-service MFA settings and the old SSPR method list. Keyword: one policy.
Passkeys (FIDO2) and certificate-based authentication. The credential is bound to the origin and never leaves the authenticator. Keyword: origin-bound.
A time-limited passcode to bootstrap a stronger method. Used for new starters with no credential and for recovery when all methods are lost. Keyword: bootstrap.
Nudges users on weaker methods toward Microsoft Authenticator during sign-in. Keyword: nudge during sign-in.
Pushes a cloud SSPR reset back to Active Directory so the on-premises password changes too. Keyword: hybrid SSPR needs it.
Global banned list plus a custom organisation list; the on-premises agent applies the same rules to domain controller password changes. Keyword: extends on-premises.
All matching policies are evaluated and the most restrictive wins. One block defeats any number of grants. Keyword: block wins.
Evaluates the policy and records what would have happened without enforcing it. The safe first step for every new policy. Keyword: measure before enforce.

front: Require all vs require one control
back: The radio button under grant controls. Choosing 'one of the selected' when you meant 'all' is the classic accidental loosening. Keyword: AND or OR.
A grant control demanding specific methods, such as phishing-resistant MFA, rather than any second factor. Keyword: which factor, not whether.
Critical events such as disable, password reset, or session revoke are pushed to services, which reject the token in near real time. Keyword: does not wait for expiry.

Sign-in risk says this authentication looks wrong — remediate with MFA. User risk says the credential is known to someone else — remediate with a password change. Keyword: prove identity vs replace credential.
Service principals get their own detections and policy type, because they cannot perform MFA and so cannot self-remediate. Keyword: no MFA available.
Private Access publishes internal apps per application instead of a VPN. Internet Access is an outbound secure web gateway with content filtering. Keyword: inbound apps vs outbound web.
The application object is the global definition in its home tenant; the service principal is the local instance that holds grants and role assignments. Keyword: definition vs instance.
System-assigned dies with its resource. User-assigned is standalone and can be shared across many resources. Keyword: shared and surviving.
Azure creates, rotates, and protects the credential, so no secret appears in code or configuration. Keyword: no stored secret.
An external issuer such as GitHub Actions exchanges its own token for an Entra token. No secret or certificate is stored anywhere. Keyword: no credential at all.
Delegated acts on behalf of a signed-in user and is limited by what that user can do. Application acts as itself with no user and always needs admin consent. Keyword: user present or not.
Declared by the application to describe its own authorisation model, assigned to users, groups, or apps, and emitted as the roles claim. Keyword: roles claim.
Turning it on means only assigned users and groups may sign in to the enterprise application. Keyword: catalogue becomes a boundary.
Publishes an on-premises web app through Entra ID using outbound-only connectors, so no inbound firewall port is opened. Keyword: outbound connectors.
A phishing page persuades a user to approve an app that then reads data with a token rather than a stolen password. Restrict user consent to stop it. Keyword: token, not password.
Turns the dead end created by disabling user consent into a request that named reviewers approve, with the decision recorded. Keyword: request instead of dead end.
Conditional Access hands the session to Defender for Cloud Apps as a reverse proxy so session policies can block download, copy, or upload in real time. Keyword: act inside the session.
Marks a discovered app as unacceptable and pushes a block to the connected enforcement point. Keyword: discovery then block.
A catalog is the container of resources and the unit of delegation. An access package bundles chosen resources and roles into one requestable item. Keyword: container vs bundle.
Decides who may request, whether approval and justification are needed, and how long the assignment lasts before expiry. Keyword: who, approval, duration.

front: Separation of duties in entitlement management
back: Blocks a user who already holds one package from requesting an incompatible one. Keyword: incompatible combination.
A partner directory or domain recognised by entitlement management so its users can request packages and be governed on a lifecycle. Keyword: external requestors.
Removes access when the access review ends. Without it the review only produces a report someone must act on. Keyword: otherwise nothing happens.
Chooses no change, remove access, approve access, or take recommendations. 'No change' is what makes a review that never removes anything. Keyword: the default is inaction.
Chains reviewers so a self-attestation is checked by a manager or owner afterwards. Keyword: second opinion.

front: Eligible vs active assignment in PIM
back: Eligible must be activated and leaves no privilege at rest. Active is standing privilege. Keyword: activate to use.
Makes membership or ownership of a group itself activatable, which brings PIM to anything grantable through a group. Keyword: extend PIM's reach.
Two cloud-only permanent Global Administrators, excluded from Conditional Access and PIM, credentials stored offline, sign-ins alerted. Keyword: excluded on purpose.
Sign-in logs for authentication attempts and applied CA policies. Audit logs for directory changes. Provisioning logs for what the provisioning service did. Keyword: three streams.
